sections.content:
You know *si* + present indicative from B1 Unit 8, *si* + imperfect subjunctive from B1 Unit 4 and *de* + infinitive from B2 Unit 10. *Si* + indicative is not only for plans. You also use it to take something as true and draw a conclusion: "if it is true that…". The speaker does not imagine the situation; they accept it.

The verb in the *si* clause can be in any indicative tense: *Si ya ha salido* (it has happened), *Si no contesta* (it is happening). The conclusion is often in the future of probability from B1 Unit 22: *estará ocupado* "he must be busy". With *si* + imperfect subjunctive you would imagine the situation instead, and that is a different sentence.

*De* + infinitive also carries a condition, and it is shorter: *De ser verdad* means *Si es verdad*.

items.spanish: Si tiene fiebre, tiene que ir al médico.
items.english: If he has a fever, he has to go to the doctor.

items.spanish: Si ya ha salido, llegará pronto.
items.english: If he has already left, he will arrive soon.
If he does not answer, he must be busy.

items.spanish: De ser necesario, te llamo mañana.
items.english: If it is necessary, I will call you tomorrow.

sections.content: *Si* never takes the present subjunctive: *si no conteste* is a mistake. With the imperfect subjunctive the sentence is imagined, not accepted as true: *Si no contestara, estaría ocupado*.
